extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, applicants, carriers, interconnected/non-interconnected VoIP providers, and other persons or entities filing pleadings, petitions, or applications with the Federal Communications Commission
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for service, format, filing, content, verification, and procedural handling of pleadings, forbearance petitions, and applications before the FCC (Part 1). Covers electronic filing (ULS/ECFS), lengths/format, proof of service, agent designation, antenna/ASR procedures, and related procedural timelines and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and completion of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Service means handing it to the party, his attorney, or other duly constituted agent; or leaving it with the clerk or other person in charge of the office of the person being served; or, if there is no one in charge of such office, leaving it in a conspicuous place therein; or, if such office is closed or the person to be served has no office, leaving it at his dwelling house or usual place of abode with some person of suitable age and discretion then residing therein. For pleadings, petitions, and other documents associated with licensing matters in the Wireless Radio Services, delivery of a copy pursuant to this section is complete by sending it by email to the email addresses listed in the ULS, or to the email address of the applicant's or licensee's attorney provided in a pleading or other document served on the filer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service by mail is complete upon mailing. Service by email is complete upon sending to the email address listed in the ULS for a particular license, application, or filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of service, as provided in this section, shall be filed before action is taken. The proof of service shall show the time and manner of service, and may be by written acknowledgement of service, by certificate of the person effecting the service, or by other proof satisfactory to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to make proof of service will not affect the validity of the service. The Commission may allow the proof to be amended or supplied at any time, unless to do so would result in material prejudice to a party. Proof of electronic service shall show the email address of the person making the service, in addition to that person's residence or business address; the date and time of the electronic service; the name and email address of the person served; and that the document was served electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of agent for service (carriers and VoIP providers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every common carrier and interconnected VoIP provider, and non-interconnected VoIP provider with interstate end-user revenues subject to contribution to the TRS Fund and subject to the Communications Act, shall designate an agent in the District of Columbia (and may designate additional agents) upon whom service of all notices, process, orders, decisions, and requirements of the Commission may be made for and on behalf of such carrier or provider in any proceeding before the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation must include name, business address, telephone/voicemail number, facsimile number, and, if available, internet email address, other names under which it does business, and, if affiliated, parent/holding/management company. File within 30 days of commencement of service with the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau's Market Disputes Resolution Division. Telecommunications Reporting Worksheet filed annually must contain designated agent info. Notify the Commission within one week of any changes. If no agent designated, service may be made by posting the notice/process/order in the Office of the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, statements, tables of contents and summaries of filings, and other materials which are submitted with and factually support a pleading are not counted in determining the length of the pleading. If other materials are submitted with a pleading, they will be counted in determining its length; and if the length of the pleadings, as so computed, is greater than permitted by the provisions of this chapter, the pleading will be returned without consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission's policy is that requests to file pleadings in excess of prescribed length shall not be routinely granted. Where the filing period is 10 days or less, the request shall be made within 2 business days after the period begins; where more than 10 days, at least 10 days before the filing date. If timely request is made, the pleading need not be filed earlier than 2 business days after Commission acts on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical format and typographical specifications for paper filings
rubrics_metrics.description: All pleadings and documents filed in paper form shall be typewritten or prepared by mechanical processing methods, and shall be filed electronically or on paper with dimensions of A4 (21 cm x 29.7 cm) or 8 1/2 x 11 inch with the margins set so that the printed material does not exceed 6 1/2 x 9 1/2 inches. The printed material may be in any typeface of at least 12-point in height. The body of the text must be double spaced with a minimum distance of 7/32 of an inch between each line of text. Footnotes and long, indented quotations may be single spaced, but must be in type that is 12-point or larger in height, with at least 1/16 of an inch between each line of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel are cautioned against employing extended single spaced passages or excessive footnotes to evade prescribed pleading lengths; if used in this manner, pleading may be rejected or dismissed with leave to refile. Pleadings may be printed on both sides; single-sided pleadings shall be stapled or bound in upper left-hand corner; double-sided shall be stapled twice or bound so it opens like a book. Exceptions include Commission-requested printed briefs, official publications, maps, original documents offered as exhibits, specially prepared exhibits, or other specific provisions. All copies shall be clearly legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents and summary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (d) of this section, all pleadings and documents filed with the Commission, the length of which as computed under this chapter exceeds ten pages, shall include, as part of the pleading or document, a table of contents with page references. They shall also include a summary of the filing, suitably paragraphed, which should be a succinct, but accurate and clear condensation of the substance of the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary should not be a mere repetition of headings. For filings exceeding ten but not twenty-five pages, the summary should seldom exceed one and never two pages; for filings exceeding twenty-five pages, the summary should seldom exceed two and never five pages. The table of contents and summary pages shall not be included in complying with any page limitation requirements. Exemptions (paragraph (d)) include interrogatories, FCC forms, transcripts, contracts/reports, letters, hearing exhibits, and exhibits/appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirements and scopes
rubrics_metrics.description: In specified types of proceedings, all pleadings (including permissible ex parte submissions, notices of ex parte presentations, comments, reply comments, and petitions for reconsideration and replies) must be filed in electronic format. A separate list identifies proceedings where electronic filing is mandatory and where it is permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory electronic filing applies to, e.g., formal complaint proceedings under section 208, CPNI proceedings (non-rulemaking), cable special relief petitions, OTA Reception Devices proceedings, certain common carrier certifications, domestic Section 214 transfer and discontinuance applications, notices of network change under §51.325 et seq., and hearing proceedings under §§1.201–1.377. Other proceedings (general rulemaking, notices of inquiry, petitions for rulemaking, petitions for forbearance, filings responsive to certain Section 214 matters and network change notices) may be filed electronically. Bureaus/Offices may expand electronic filing capabilities. For length compliance, an electronic document's length equals the printed length per paragraph (a) or may be calculated as no more than 250 words per page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's preference is for briefs that are typewritten, prepared by mechanical processing methods, or, in the Wireless Radio Services, composed electronically and sent via ULS. Printed briefs will be accepted only if specifically requested by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typewritten, mechanically produced, or electronically transmitted briefs must conform to all applicable specifications for pleadings and documents set forth in § 1.49.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of copies and electronic filing copy rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In hearing proceedings, all pleadings, letters, documents, or other written submissions shall be filed using the Commission's Electronic Comment Filing System, excluding confidential material as set forth in § 1.314. In matters other than rulemaking and hearing cases, unless otherwise specified, an original and one copy shall be filed. Where statute or regulation provides for service by the Commission of papers filed with the Commission, an additional copy shall be filed for each person to be served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parties may be required to file additional copies on notice. For application and licensing matters in Wireless Radio Services, filings must be electronic in ULS. Participants filing electronically in ULS need only submit one copy so long as submission conforms to procedural/electronic comment requirements. Electronic filings by a party represented by an attorney shall include the attorney's name, street address, email, and telephone. Parties not represented must provide their name, street address, email, and telephone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription, signature, and verification of filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The original of all petitions, motions, pleadings, briefs, and other documents filed by any party represented by counsel shall be signed by at least one attorney of record in his individual name, whose address shall be stated. A party who is not represented by an attorney shall sign and verify the document and state his address. Pleadings, petitions, and other documents related to licensing matters in the Wireless Radio Services shall be signed by at least one attorney of record in his individual name or by the party who is not represented and shall include his email and physical mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either the original document, an electronic reproduction containing the facsimile signature, or an electronic filing via ULS is acceptable. If a facsimile or electronic reproduction is filed, the signatory shall retain the original until the Commission's decision is final and no longer subject to judicial review. A signature will be considered any symbol executed or adopted by the party with intent that such symbol be a signature, including computer-generated electronic impulses. Except when otherwise provided, documents signed by the attorney need not be verified or accompanied by affidavit. The signature by an attorney constitutes a certificate that he has read the document, that to the best of his knowledge there is good ground to support it, and that it is not interposed for delay. Unsigned or sham-signed originals may be stricken and the matter proceed as though not filed. An attorney may be subjected to disciplinary action for willful violation or insertion of scandalous/indecent matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate pleading and identification for petitions for forbearance
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered as a petition for forbearance subject to the one-year deadline under 47 U.S.C. 160(c), any petition requesting that the Commission exercise its forbearance authority shall be filed as a separate pleading and shall be identified in the caption as a petition for forbearance under 47 U.S.C. 160(c). Any request not in compliance is deemed not to constitute a petition pursuant to 47 U.S.C. 160(c) and is not subject to the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner may withdraw or narrow a forbearance petition without Commission approval only by filing a notice within ten business days after the due date for reply comments; otherwise withdrawal/narrowing requires Commission approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and content requirements for petitions for forbearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for forbearance must identify the requested relief, including: (1) each statutory provision, rule, or requirement from which forbearance is sought; (2) each carrier or group of carriers for which forbearance is sought; (3) each service for which forbearance is sought; (4) each geographic location, zone, or area for which forbearance is sought; and (5) any other factor, condition, or limitation relevant to determining the scope of the requested relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must contain facts and arguments which, if true and persuasive, are sufficient to meet each statutory criterion for forbearance and must specify how each statutory criterion is met with regard to each provision. If relying on third-party data, the petition must identify the nature of the data, parties believed to have/control it, and its relation to facts and arguments, and must at filing provide a copy of the petition to each third party identified. Petitions must also identify related pending matters or declare none. Filings must comply with § 1.49. Petitions shall be e-mailed to forbearance@fcc.gov at the time of filing and all filings must be provided in searchable format (spreadsheets manipulable for analysis). Contents must include a plain concise summary of relief sought, a full statement of the prima facie case for relief, and appendices listing scope of relief, all supporting data including market analysis, and supporting statements or affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice, motions, circulation, voting, and procedural timing for forbearance petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a petition for forbearance initiates the statutory time limit for consideration. The Commission will issue a public notice when it receives a properly filed petition for forbearance which will include a statement of the nature and scope of the petition, the docket number, and the time for filing oppositions/comments and replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents may submit motions for summary denial if the petition cannot meet statutory criteria even viewed in petitioner's favor; such motions must be filed by the due date for comments. Oppositions to motions for summary denial may not be filed later than the due date for reply comments; no reply may be filed to an opposition to a motion for summary denial. If a petition includes novel questions of fact, law or policy not resolvable under precedent, the Chairperson will circulate a draft order no later than 28 days prior to the statutory deadline (unless Commissioners agree to shorter), and the Commission will vote on circulated orders not later than seven days before the last day that action must be taken to avoid grant by operation of law. The prohibition on contacts with decisionmakers concerning Sunshine Agenda matters (§1.1203(a)) applies to forbearance petitions for a period of 14 days prior to the statutory deadline. Withdrawal/narrowing rules are in §1.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antenna Structure Registration (ASR) and FAA coordination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each antenna structure owner that must notify the FAA using Form 7460-1 shall, upon proposing new or modified construction, register that antenna structure with the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau using FCC Form 854. The Bureau will address any environmental concerns prior to processing the registration in accordance with §1.1307 and §17.4(c). If a final FAA determination of 'no hazard' is not submitted with FCC Form 854, processing may be delayed or disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If owner cannot file Form 854 because of denial of Federal benefits, the first licensee authorized to locate on the structure must register using FCC Form 854 and provide copy of FCC Form 854R to the owner; owner remains responsible for providing copy to tenant licensees and posting registration number as required. Upon receipt of Form 854 and attached FAA final determination, the Bureau may prescribe painting/lighting or other conditions per FAA recommendation, and returns completed FCC Form 854R or advises registrant if disapproved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Bureau processing of applications requiring ASR
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operating Bureau or Office examines applications for Commission authorization for compliance with FAA notification and Commission ASR requirements. If ASR is required, the operating Bureau reviews for the Antenna Structure Registration Number and: (i) if application contains the ASR number or applicant seeks Cellular/PCS authorization, process the application; (ii) if application lacks ASR number but owner has filed Form 854, place application on hold until registration confirmed if owner exhibits due diligence; (iii) if application lacks ASR number and owner has not filed Form 854, notify applicant that Form 854 must be filed and place application on hold until registration can be confirmed if owner exhibits due diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ASR is not required, the operating Bureau processes the application. For antenna farm areas, applications proposing structures over 1,000 feet above ground will not be accepted unless (1) proposed in designated antenna farm area, or (2) accompanied by FAA statement that structure will not constitute menace to air navigation, or (3) accompanied by waiver request with sufficient reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption and burden regarding very tall antenna towers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for antenna towers higher than 2,000 feet above ground will be presumed to be inconsistent with the public interest, and the applicant will have a burden of overcoming that strong presumption. The applicant must accompany its application with a detailed showing directed to meeting this burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only in exceptional cases, where a clear and compelling showing is made that there are public interest reasons requiring a tower higher than 2,000 feet, and after compliance with FAA procedures and full Commission coordination with FAA on menace to air navigation, will a grant be made. Applicants and parties in interest will be afforded statutory hearing rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation pending action on renewal application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is pending before the Commission at the time of expiration of license any proper and timely application for renewal with respect to any activity of a continuing nature, such license shall continue in effect without further action by the Commission until the Commission makes a final determination with respect to the renewal application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No operation under this provision is a finding that operation will serve the public interest. A non-broadcast licensee operating by virtue of this paragraph shall, after the date of expiration, post in addition to the original license any acknowledgement received that the renewal application has been accepted for filing or a signed copy of the renewal application submitted, or in services other than common carrier, a statement certifying that the licensee has mailed or filed a renewal application specifying date of mailing/filing. For non-continuing activities, Commission may grant temporary extension pending determination. Except where authorization clearly relates to non-continuing activity, all licenses are deemed related to continuing activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to amend and report substantial or significant changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant is responsible for continuing accuracy and completeness of information furnished in a pending application or in Commission proceedings involving a pending application. Whenever the information in the pending application is no longer substantially accurate and complete in all significant respects, the applicant shall as promptly as possible and in any event within 30 days, unless good cause shown, amend or request amendment of the application to furnish additional or corrected information as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there has been a substantial change as to any other matter of decisional significance in a proceeding involving the pending application, the applicant shall within 30 days submit a statement furnishing such additional or corrected information and serve it upon parties of record in accordance with §1.47. Where matter is before any court for review, statements and requests to amend shall also be served upon the Commission's General Counsel. For purposes of this section, 'pending' means from acceptance for filing until grant/denial no longer subject to reconsideration or review. Broadcast permittees/licensees must report annually any adverse finding or adverse final action by any court or administrative body involving conduct bearing on character qualifications as reflected in renewal form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on application for license to cover construction permit
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for license by the lawful holder of a construction permit will be granted without hearing where the Commission, upon examination of such application, finds that all the terms, conditions, and obligations set forth in the application and permit have been fully met, and that no cause or circumstance arising or first coming to the knowledge of the Commission since the granting of the permit would make the operation of such station against the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commission is unable to make those findings, the Commission will designate the application for hearing upon specified issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference to service-specific application procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The general application procedures set forth in §§ 1.61 through 1.68 are general in nature and applicants should also refer to Commission rules regarding payment of statutory charges and use of the FCC Registration Number (FRN). More detailed procedures are set out in other parts and subparts for specific services (e.g., Broadcast Radio Services, Common Carrier Radio Services, Private Radio Services, Experimental Radio Service, Domestic Public Radio Services, equipment certification, commercial radio operator licenses, terrestrial microwave services, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the referenced subparts and parts for rules that govern applications specific to those services.
